name: Nelson Mandela
role: Anti-apartheid leader; President of South Africa (1994–1999)
summary: Mandela was an African nationalist and self-described socialist who moved from nonviolent protest to armed struggle against apartheid and later led a negotiated transition to multiracial democracy. As president he put reconciliation, a non-racial national identity and expanded social services first, while keeping a largely market-oriented economic framework.

universal-healthcare.rationale: His government made public care free for children under six and pregnant women in 1994 and extended free primary care in 1996; he stopped short of a stated universal scheme in these sources.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources consulted.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Called himself a socialist, yet as president kept a liberal framework, adopted the market-oriented GEAR policy and courted private investment. His mature position is mixed and contested.

public-ownership.rationale: At Rivonia he backed the Freedom Charter's nationalisation of mines, banks and monopoly industry. As president he downplayed nationalisation and began privatisation, so his mature view is ambiguous.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: In 1994 he said a permanently higher general level of taxation should be avoided while pledging redistribution. No specific position on taxing the rich was found.

unions-good.rationale: Urged that labour be treated 'as a resource and not a cost' and called for labour-law reform through cooperation between government, labour and business.

property-fundamental.rationale: Supported redistribution of land (not nationalisation) within a private-enterprise economy, and his government passed land reform protecting tenants. This is neither strong protection of property nor rejection of it.

regulate-corporations.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources consulted.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare spending rose under his government and racially differentiated grants were equalised.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Pledged to deracialise the economy and correct apartheid spending patterns, set up the TRC, and pursued land reform.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Promoted a shared 'Rainbow Nation' identity, embraced Afrikaner symbols such as the Springboks and Ingrid Jonker, and praised Xhosa traditional governance. This is inferred rather than a stated position.

gradual-change.rationale: After decades of revolutionary struggle he led a negotiated transition, a unity government and reconciliation, and kept existing economic institutions. The record points both ways.

reduce-immigration.rationale: As president he urged South Africans to welcome illegal migrants as 'brothers and sisters'.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: In 2003 he accused Bush of undermining the UN and said he would back UN-authorised action without reservation; he also said human rights should be the core of international relations.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: He would support UN-authorised action against Iraq and backed the 1998 Lesotho intervention, but opposed the NATO Kosovo intervention and the Iraq war. His position depended on context.

notes: Died 5 December 2013 (born 18 July 1918). His economic views shifted: he backed Freedom Charter nationalisation in the 1950s–60s, but as president he adopted GEAR and some privatisation. Answers use his mature record where it exists. On violence he moved from nonviolence to armed struggle and then to negotiation; the answers reflect his consistent defence of the armed struggle against apartheid. Many statements concern topics he never addressed publicly (drugs, sex work, gender theory, technology, currency, ecology) and are left null rather than inferred from ANC positions.
